title: Birds and Beaks
checkpoint: Year 1 Autumn 1, week 2 — School readiness — Phase 5: new sounds ea, oy, ir
note_for_grown_ups: Non-fiction, Phase 5, 82-sound stage (ea, oy, ir just added).

pages.text: Ned sits near the dirt path.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling sitting at the edge of a bare dirt path.

pages.text: A bird can peck at the dirt.
pages.illustration: A small garden bird pecking at the dark dirt of the path.

pages.text: The bird has a long beak.
pages.illustration: Close view of a small bird's long, thin beak.

pages.text: The beak digs in the dirt.
pages.illustration: The bird's long beak pushed down into the loose dirt.
The bird lifting its beak with a small bug held inside it.
The small bird swallowing the bug, clearly pleased with its meal.

pages.text: Birds and ducks like a good meal.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling and the small bird side by side, both looking content.

pages.text: Ned has a beak too, but it is flat.
pages.illustration: Close view of Ned the duckling's own flat, wide bill.

pages.text: A flat beak is good for the pond.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling dipping his flat bill into the shallow pond water.

pages.text: Each bird has a beak that helps it eat.
pages.illustration: Ned the duckling and the small bird eating side by side near the path.
